newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes near low after bumpy ride.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes near low after bumpy ride.

text.p: IPE gas oil last traded down $5.25 and just off the lows on Tuesday after a technical sell-off on NYMEX triggered aggressive long liquidation, traders said.
Feb gas oil's late slide to $213.75 a tonne dismantled a brief recovery from a dramatic mid-afternoon slump to the low $213.50, in a partial replay of gas oil's $7.25 fall on Monday.
"The last two days have seen determined long liquidation. Today the technical signals in London and New York toppled the market," a trader said.
Traders said continuing mild weather in Europe added to gas oil's late weakness in relation to Brent, which staged a recovery around the gas oil close.

Feb Brent was trading at $23.38 a barrel at 1752 GMT, 18 cents of the intra-day low of $23.20. Minutes before the mid-afternoon slump Brent had traded at a session high of $23.55 on the back of an aborted upside break by NYMEX crude and products.
U.S. regional forecasters expect temperatures to rise this week before another cold spell this weekend in the "heating oil belt" of the Northeastern U.S.
The next cue for the market would come from weekly U.S. inventory figures to be released by the American Petroleum Institute (API) after the close of trade today, brokers said.
